title: The Unquiet Verdict
premise: When the coffin of Aldous Merrick, founder of the fog-bound town of Verity Hollow, is exhumed for a centennial ceremony and found empty, retired detective Paloma Kavanagh is dragged back into investigative work by a desperate town council. The only person who could explain the empty grave is Nell Ashcombe, the star witness of a forty-year-old verdict that sent an innocent man to prison — and who everyone insists died decades ago. As Paloma follows a trail of forged death certificates, buried ledgers, and loyal silences, he discovers the town's founding families have protected a living lie for two generations, and that someone is now killing to keep it buried. In the end, Paloma finds Nell alive in hiding, forces the truth into the open at great personal cost, and must choose between the loyalty of old friends and a justice the law can no longer deliver.
about_author: Isandro Villalobos is a former small-town court clerk turned novelist who writes mysteries about the secrets communities keep to survive. He lives near the coast, where he collects local histories and insists every legend has a paper trail.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Paper
chapters.summary: Paloma Kavanagh's POV. In his failing bookshop, Paloma catalogues unsold stock and dodges the town's pity, clinging to his pride in cases closed. A council delegation arrives: Aldous Merrick's coffin will be exhumed for the centennial reinterment, and they want Paloma present as a formality. Emotional beat: restlessness, the itch of an unopened case.

chapters.title: What the Grave Gave Back
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV at the cemetery. The coffin is opened before the gathered town and contains only river stones and a rotted coat belonging to no one. The crowd's grief curdles into fear; the priest faints; the council goes pale. Paloma notices fresh tool marks on the vault door. Emotional beat: shock hardening into professional hunger.

chapters.title: Forty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Digging through his old case files, Paloma rereads the trial that made his reputation: the drowning of Merrick's business partner, convicted on the testimony of witness Nell Ashcombe — declared dead five years later. He remembers her testimony never quite fit. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing like a body in water.

chapters.title: The Council of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: councilwoman Beatrice Voss. Beatrice privately urges the mayor to shut down the investigation and cremate the 'remains' quietly. We glimpse her burning a letter and lying to her grown son about the family's role in the founding. Emotional beat: dread beneath civic composure.

chapters.title: A Witness, Presumed
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At the records office, Paloma finds Nell's death certificate signed by a doctor who died before the date on it. Someone paid for the paperwork. His first anonymous threat arrives, pinned to the bookshop door with a funeral card bearing his own name. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing he is hunted.

chapters.title: Ledgers in the Flood
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Following Merrick's financial trail, Paloma discovers the founder's fortune was built on smuggled labor contracts — and that the drowned partner knew. The old conviction begins to look like a murder arranged by the town itself. Emotional beat: disillusionment with the legend he grew up believing.

chapters.title: Tea with the Widow
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He interviews Merrick's ancient widow, who serves tea and tells him, sweetly, that some coffins are empty because some men never deserved to be in them. She slips him a key hidden in a sugar bowl. Emotional beat: eerie complicity; the first ally inside the lie.

chapters.title: The Key to Room Nine
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The key opens a locker in the defunct railway station containing Nell's real diary and a photograph of her taken years after her supposed death. Someone has been checking the locker as recently as last month. Emotional beat: hope sharpening into urgency.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Loyal
chapters.summary: POV: Tomás Reyes, the constable. Tomás, who owes Paloma his career, is ordered by the mayor to surveil him. Torn, he falsifies his reports but warns Paloma obliquely over drinks. Emotional beat: loyalty bending under institutional pressure.

chapters.title: The Second Body
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The records clerk who processed Nell's certificate is found drowned in the reservoir — the same method as the original murder. Paloma realizes the killer is replaying history, erasing the same trail twice. Emotional beat: cold terror; the past is not past.

chapters.title: Confessions at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Beatrice Voss, rattled by the murder, half-confesses: the founding families covered up the partner's killing to protect Merrick, and Nell fled rather than recant or stay silent. She doesn't know where Nell went — but her son might. Emotional beat: shame breaking loyalty's dam.

chapters.title: The Son Who Kept the Books
chapters.summary: POV: Elias Voss. Elias, who inherited the family ledgers, confronts his mother, then secretly copies pages implicating the current mayor's father. He mails them to Paloma and immediately regrets it. Emotional beat: a young man choosing truth over inheritance.

chapters.title: Fire in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The bookshop burns overnight; the diary survives only because Paloma slept in the back room. Among the ashes he finds a boot print matching the constable's spare pair — someone inside his circle. Emotional beat: betrayal cutting deeper than loss.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Firelight
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma corners Tomás, who breaks down: he was ordered to watch, not burn, and he can prove the mayor's aide took the ledgers' twin copy. The two men form an uneasy alliance outside the law. Emotional beat: wounded trust cautiously rebuilt.

chapters.title: The Mayor's Quiet Hour
chapters.summary: POV: Mayor Corliss Hale. Hale burns documents in his study and makes a call arranging a boat for Friday night. We learn he has known Nell lived for years and has been paying for her silence — until she stopped answering. Emotional beat: panic dressed as control.

chapters.title: Following the Tide Chart
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Decoding marginalia in Nell's diary, Paloma maps her old smuggling routes and deduces she lives at the derelict lighthouse on Cutter's Point, reachable only at low tide — which falls Friday night. The same night as the mayor's boat. Emotional beat: racing clarity.

chapters.title: Nell Ashcombe, Alive
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At the lighthouse, Paloma finds Nell — old, sharp, unrepentant. She confesses she saw Merrick kill his partner and was coerced into testifying against an innocent man; her faked death was her only escape. She refuses to come forward: 'The verdict kept me alive.' Emotional beat: moral vertigo — the truth-teller who chose silence.

chapters.title: Friday Night, Falling Water
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The mayor's men arrive at the point to finish what the fire started. Paloma, Nell, and Tomás are trapped by the rising tide in a standoff among the rocks. Shots are fired; Tomás takes a wound shielding Nell. Emotional beat: siege desperation, tide as clock.

chapters.title: The Unquiet Verdict
chapters.summary: Climax, Paloma's POV. Paloma turns the trap: he recorded the mayor's aide confessing to both drownings, and broadcasts it over the lighthouse radio to the whole town, gathered for the centennial reinterment below the cliffs. The mayor's men stand down as headlights flood the causeway. Emotional beat: catharsis — justice spoken aloud where everyone can hear.

chapters.title: Reinterment
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The mayor is arrested; the innocent man's conviction is posthumously vacated. At the delayed ceremony, the town buries the stones from the coffin alongside a formal apology read aloud. Nell watches from the back, unnamed. Emotional beat: public reckoning, private absolution incomplete.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Owes
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Nell asks Paloma why he didn't turn her in for perjury. He answers that the law got its verdict wrong once already; he won't compound it. She gives him her full statement anyway — her choice, freely made. Emotional beat: reconciliation between memory and truth.

chapters.title: Open for Business
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, epilogue. Weeks later, the bookshop reopens with new shelves and a hand-lettered sign: CLOSED CASES CONSULTED. A stranger leaves a sealed envelope on the counter — a new mystery. Paloma, smiling despite himself, locks the door and opens it. Emotional beat: renewal; the detective's hunger answered.
